title: University of Sussex spinout Universal Quantum raises “record” $100M Series A
key_facts: Universal Quantum, a University of Sussex spinout founded in 2018, has raised $100m in a Series A round, which the company says is the largest Series A raised by a UK-headquartered quantum firm.
The round was co-led by DCVC, a Silicon Valley venture firm, and Firgun Ventures, a quantum-focused investor.
Other investors include EDBI, the Singapore-based sovereign investor, and Dave Baszucki, founder and CEO of Roblox.
Sebastian Weidt, CEO and co-founder of Universal Quantum, says the round unites investors around a single mission: delivering utility-scale quantum computing.

The company has raised over $125m in total; in 2023 it was awarded a €67 million contract from the German Aerospace Center (DLR), which the article calls the largest ever granted to a UK-based quantum startup.
The new money will fund expansion in the United States, Japan and its German hub in Hamburg, plus commercialisation of the technology.
Company claims, not independently checked in the text: chips are made on a standard 200mm commercial foundry line and the machines can run at room temperature.
quote_evidence: Universal Quantum’s progress reflects our partners’ belief that we represent one of the most credible paths to quantum computing at scale.

Universal Quantum will use the funding to speed up its global expansion in the United States, Japan and across its German hub in Hamburg, as well as the development and commercialisation of its technology, it said.
why_it_matters_hint: A large private funding round for a UK quantum start-up; the record and scale claims are the company's own.
